correctness.rationale: Each law was reconstructed from the exact standardized event. Gamma uses the small-threshold expansion of the upper incomplete gamma ratio: with threshold \(\alpha+y\sqrt\alpha\), \(1/\Gamma(\alpha)=\alpha+O(\alpha^2)\) and \(-\log(\alpha+y\sqrt\alpha)=\frac12\log(1/\alpha)-\log y+o(1)\), giving the displayed Euler-constant correction. The exact Pareto tail gives \(\varepsilon/(2y^2)\). For Weibull, the standard deviation dominates the mean and Stirling gives \(\alpha(\mu+y\sigma)^{\alpha}\to2/e\). The log-normal threshold is \(\sigma+(\log y)/\sigma+o(1/\sigma)\), and Mills' ratio yields the stated Gaussian-in-log-scale equivalent. For \(\operatorname{Beta}(1,q)\), the exact survival expression expands to the claimed half-logarithmic term. Independent high-precision checks for several fixed positive \(y\) values approach each asymptotic ratio as predicted.
